title: Java Math
learningObjectives: Use the Math class for common numeric operations.
Apply Math.max and Math.min to compare numeric values.
Use Math.sqrt and Math.abs for square-root and absolute-value calculations.
Distinguish rounding with Math.round from truncation by casting.
Use Math.floor, Math.ceil and Math.pow where their behaviour is appropriate.

understand.concept: The java.lang.Math class provides static methods and constants for common mathematical operations. It includes methods for comparing values, calculating powers and square roots, taking absolute values and rounding floating-point values.
understand.whyItMatters: Math operations are useful for measurements, scoring, geometry, finance-related calculations and data processing. Using established library methods is clearer than recreating common formulas.
understand.analogy: The Math class is like a well-tested toolbox: each method performs a familiar operation with documented input and output rules.
understand.analogyLimit: A toolbox does not decide whether a formula is appropriate for a particular domain. Floating-point results can have rounding error, and Math methods do not replace domain-specific validation.

explain.narrative:
## The Math class

Math is part of `java.lang`, which is imported automatically. Its common methods are static, so call them using the class name:

```java
double root = Math.sqrt(81);
int larger = Math.max(12, 20);
```

## Common methods

- `Math.max(a, b)` returns the greater of two values.
- `Math.min(a, b)` returns the smaller value.
- `Math.abs(value)` returns an absolute value.
- `Math.sqrt(value)` returns the non-negative square root for a non-negative input; a negative input produces NaN.
- `Math.pow(base, exponent)` raises a value to a power and returns a double.
- `Math.round(value)` rounds to the nearest integer result type (long for double input, int for float input).
- `Math.floor(value)` returns the greatest integral-valued double not greater than the input.
- `Math.ceil(value)` returns the least integral-valued double not less than the input.

## Rounding is not casting

Casting a double to int truncates toward zero. Math.round uses nearest-integer rounding with ties toward positive infinity. Math.floor and Math.ceil have different directional rules. Choose the operation that matches the requirement rather than assuming all of them mean round.

## Floating-point caution

Most decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly in binary floating-point. Do not compare calculated doubles for exact equality when a tolerance-based comparison is more appropriate. For exact decimal financial arithmetic, consider BigDecimal with an explicit rounding policy.

## Common mistakes

- Calling a static Math method through an instance unnecessarily.
- Assuming Math.sqrt accepts negative values and returns a real number.
- Confusing floor, ceil, round and an integer cast.
- Expecting Math.pow to return an int.
- Treating floating-point results as exact decimal values.

examples.title: Compare and calculate
examples.explanation: The static methods return the larger value, smaller value and square root. sqrt returns a double.

examples.title: Rounding methods
examples.explanation: round returns the nearest integer result, floor moves down to an integral-valued double, ceil moves up, and abs removes the sign.

practise.guidedTask: Use Math.max and Math.min to compare two test scores. Use Math.sqrt to calculate the square root of a perfect square and print each result.
practise.independentTask: Given a measured distance as a double, print its absolute value and demonstrate the difference between Math.round, Math.floor and Math.ceil for a positive decimal.
hints: Math methods are called with the Math class name.
sqrt and pow return double values.
A cast to int truncates; it is not the same as Math.round.
practise.challenge: For a negative decimal such as -4.6, compare Math.round, Math.floor and Math.ceil. Explain why their results differ.

questions.prompt: Which method returns the greater of two values?
questions.explanation: Math.max returns the larger of its two arguments.
The square root of 64 is 8, returned as a double.

questions.prompt: Which method rounds 4.6 to the nearest integer?
questions.explanation: Math.round rounds to the nearest integer result type.
floor returns the greatest integral-valued double less than or equal to the input.
Math.abs returns the non-negative magnitude of the value.
